Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from Arkansas statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

Arkansas property tax is assessed and collected at the local level, and owners can appeal an assessment. Here is what the official sources say.

What the official sources say

  • The third Monday in August is the deadline to file an appeal with the county Board of Equalization. (Arkansas Assessment Coordination Division | DFA; source)
  • The assessment rate is 20% of true, actual, or market value (Ark. Code Ann. 26-26-303(c)). (Arkansas Property Tax FAQs (DFA); source)
  • Market value is determined as of the January 1 valuation date of the tax year. (Arkansas Property Tax FAQs (DFA); source)
  • Taxes are due from the first business day in March through October 15 of the year following the assessment year; a 10% penalty applies if not paid by then. (Arkansas Property Tax FAQs (DFA); source)
  • Amendment 79 caps annual increases in taxable value after reappraisal at 5% for homesteads and 10% for other real property, until full assessed value is reached. (Property Tax Relief | DFA; source)
  • At least 30 calendar days before an in-person tax-delinquent auction, the Commissioner of State Lands notifies the owner and interested parties by regular mail of the right to redeem. (26 CAR 400-106; source)
  • Redemption must be received before 4:00 p.m. CT on the last business day before the sale, by paying taxes, penalties, interest, fees, and costs. (26 CAR 400-106; source)
Selling in Arkansas?
We buy Arkansas houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What we could not confirm

  • Details we could not confirm on an official page are not stated.

How to sell a Arkansas house when this applies to you

  1. Find out what the title company needs. For an inherited or transferred house, that usually means the recorded deed or the probate paperwork that shows who owns it today.
  2. Get a payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See we buy houses in Arkansas.

What a cash sale of a Arkansas house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in Arkansas.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.
  2. Get a written cash offer. We review the details and send a written offer. There is no obligation, and you can turn it down and owe us nothing.
  3. Pick your closing date. You choose the timeline. Some owners need weeks to move out, and others want to close quickly.
  4. The title company handles the paperwork. It checks ownership, pays off any mortgage and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds, and records the deed.
  5. You receive the proceeds. Our offers carry no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs to you.

Documents and information to have ready

You do not need everything below to get an offer, but each item makes the sale smoother and helps the title company work faster.

  • The deed or other proof of who owns the property today.
  • A recent mortgage statement or a payoff figure from the lender.
  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.
  • Estate paperwork, such as letters from the court, if you inherited the house.
  • A short list of known repairs. We buy as-is, but honest information avoids surprises.

Listing, selling it yourself or a cash offer: how they compare

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required Arkansas disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

Questions to ask before you sell in Arkansas

  • Ask the title company what is owed and what the title company will need at closing.
  • Ask your lender for a written payoff figure good through your expected closing date, and ask whether there is a prepayment penalty.
  • Ask the county assessor whether a pending appeal or exemption affects the bill, and whether any exemption you receive ends when you sell.
  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

These are general questions to start a conversation, not legal advice. Rules in Arkansas change, so confirm details with the official office or a Arkansas attorney or tax professional.

More questions about selling in Arkansas

How fast can I close on a cash sale?

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

Do I have to clean out or repair the house?

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Will you buy a house that has tenants in it?

Yes. We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the lease when you request an offer.

What if I owe more on the mortgage than the house is worth?

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished?

It depends on who has legal authority to sign. The title company can tell you what court paperwork it needs.

Is there any cost to request an offer?

No. Requesting an offer is free and carries no obligation.

What happens to unpaid property tax when I sell?

The closing agent pays unpaid tax from the sale proceeds at closing.

  • A freeze does not pass to a subsequent owner of the same home; a buyer cannot claim the seller's prior limitation. (Property Tax Relief | DFA; source)
  • The October 15 deadline applies to filing the Homestead Credit Application. (Arkansas Assessment Coordination Division | DFA; source)
  • Property owners may claim only one homestead tax credit each year. (Property Tax Relief | DFA; source)

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from Arkansas statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

Arkansas evictions follow notice and court steps set by state law. Here is what the official sources say.

What the official sources say

  • Failure to pay rent, or to pay on time, is grounds for eviction; a landlord may bring a civil 'unlawful detainer' action. (Landlord And Tenant Rights | Arkansas AG; source)
  • Unlawful detainer requires three days' written notice to vacate before the landlord files suit. (Landlord And Tenant Rights | Arkansas AG; source)
  • After receiving a summons, the tenant has five days to object in writing to the clerk; without an objection the sheriff can remove the tenant, and with one a hearing is scheduled. (Landlord And Tenant Rights | Arkansas AG; source)
  • Property left in the dwelling at lease termination is considered abandoned and may be disposed of by the landlord. (Landlord And Tenant Rights | Arkansas AG; source)
  • A landlord may terminate a lease for any reason, giving one rental period's notice for an oral lease or notice per the terms of a written lease. (Landlord And Tenant Rights | Arkansas AG; source)
  • Landlords must give notice of at least one rental period before raising rent. (Landlord And Tenant Rights | Arkansas AG; source)
  • The security-deposit law applies only to landlords who rent six or more dwellings; deposits are capped at two months' rent and must be returned within 60 days of vacating. (Landlord And Tenant Rights | Arkansas AG; source)

A Arkansas deed is recorded with the county office named in the sources below. Here is what the official sources say.

What the official sources say

  • Quitclaim deeds given between divorcing parties as a division of marital property are exempt from the transfer tax. (26 CAR 166-102; source)
  • A quitclaim deed to a lienholder given to avoid foreclosure is exempt from the transfer tax. (26 CAR 166-102; source)
  • The transfer tax applies to each deed or instrument conveying realty, at $3.30 per $1,000 of consideration over $100. (Real Property Transfer Tax | DFA; source)
  • The Circuit Clerk acts as ex-officio recorder and serves as the Land Recorder for the county (Greene County example). (Circuit Clerk | Greene County; source)
  • A beneficiary deed must be recorded before the owner's death in the office of the county recorder where the property is located. (Act 243 of 2007; source)
  • DFA sells real estate transfer stamps and publishes an Affidavit of Compliance form for the transfer tax. (Real Property Transfer Tax | DFA; source)

  • Act 423 of 2021 amends Ark. Code 28-41-101(a): a distributee may collect and distribute a small estate without a personal representative when no petition for appointment is pending or granted. (Act 423 of 2021 (arkleg.state.ar.us); source)
